judged_text: The blacklist and existing-attendee dedup filters use exact string equality while blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com', and a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is not deduplicated. Blacklisted addresses receive event emails/ICS invites by simply varying case, and case-variant duplicates of existing attendees are inserted as new attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The blacklist and existing-attendee dedup filters use exact string equality while blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased, so 'Spam@x.com' bypasses a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com', and a guest differing only in case from an existing attendee is not deduplicated. Blacklisted addresses receive event emails/ICS invites by simply varying case, and case-variant duplicates of existing attendees are inserted as new attendee rows, producing duplicate emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the incoming `guest` strings are not lowercased before checks: the filter uses `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. This makes both the blacklist check and existing-attendee dedup case-sensitive, allowing `Spam@x.com` to bypass a `spam@x.com` blacklist entry and allowing case-variant duplicates of existing attendee emails to be inserted via `attendees.createMany`.
